stem:
A student investigates the relationship between the luminosity *L* of a star and its mass *M* for a set of stars known as main-sequence stars.

It is suggested that *L* and *M* are related by the equation

*L* = *SZM*ⁿ

where *S* is the luminosity of the Sun, and *Z* and *n* are constants.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of lg *L* on the y-axis against lg *M* on the x-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and y-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *M* and *L* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Calculate and record values of lg (*M* / 10³⁰ kg) and lg (*L* / 10²⁸ W) in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in lg (*M* / 10³⁰ kg).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Plot a graph of lg (*L* / 10²⁸ W) against lg (*M* / 10³⁰ kg). Include error bars for lg (*M* / 10³⁰ kg).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the y-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *n* and *Z*. Include the absolute uncertainties in your values. You need not be concerned with units.

Data: *S* = 3.85 × 10²⁶ W

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Another main-sequence star has a mass of 3.0 × 10³⁰ kg.

Determine the luminosity *L* of this star.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for mass, luminosity, and their logarithms, containing six mass and luminosity values and blank cells for the logarithms.
A blank graph grid with lg (*L* / 10²⁸ W) on the vertical axis and lg (*M* / 10³⁰ kg) on the horizontal axis.

problems: part d: numeric part needs answer {symbol, unit} (either may be null)
